# dsh-block-placeholder-edits
English | 中文
Models have a habit that quietly wrecks files. They write `// ... existing code ...` in place of cod
e they didn't feel like retyping, and the edit tool takes it literally. The file now holds a comment
where forty lines of real code used to be. You only find out when the build breaks, or worse, when
y lines of real code used to be. You only find out when the build breaks, or worse, when it doesn't.
This DeepSeek Harness plugin checks every `write` and `edit` before it lands. If the new text uses a
placeholder comment to stand in for code, or a whole-file write throws away most of a large file, t
he call is refused and the file is left alone. The model is told exactly which line was the problem:

## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `
headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin
list, so add it to every profile you use. It turns on as soon as it's installed. Remove it with `ds
h plugin --profile web remove dsh-block-placeholder-edits`.
### From a clone
To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

## What counts as a placeholder
These are comments, in any common comment style (`//`, `#`, `/* */`, ``, `--`, `;`, JSX `{/* */}`),
that talk about code instead of being code:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A bare `...` line counts too, except in Python, Markdown and other files where `...` means something
bare `...` line counts too, except in Python, Markdown and other files where `...` means something.
Ordinary comments pass, including ones that mention existing code. A placeholder that was already in
the old text also doesn't count, so the plugin won't nag the model about a file that already had on
he old text also doesn't count, so the plugin won't nag the model about a file that already had one.
The second check is for whole-file `write` calls. If a file of 40 lines or more is replaced with les
s than half as many lines, the write is refused. That pattern almost always means the model rewrote
the file from memory and dropped a chunk. Targeted edits aren't affected by this check, and neither
memory and dropped a chunk. Targeted edits aren't affected by this check, and neither are new files.
## When the model means it
Sometimes deleting most of a file is the point. The model is told it can repeat the identical call o
nce to confirm, and the second try goes through. That keeps a real refactor from getting stuck, but
the model has to choose it on purpose. If you'd rather have a person decide, set `mode: ask`.
## Settings
The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-block-placeholder-edits**, change what
you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.
Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.y
ml` for all profiles. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.
